content: Biodiversity encompasses the variety of life at all levelsâgenetic diversity within species, species diversity within communities, and ecosystem diversity across landscapes. This diversity results from billions of years of evolution and provides numerous benefits to ecosystems and humans. Species diversity contributes to ecosystem stability through functional redundancyâwhen multiple species perform similar roles, the system can continue functioning if some species decline. Diverse ecosystems generally show greater resilience to disturbances like disease outbreaks, extreme weather, and climate change. This resilience stems from various mechanisms: diverse plant communities can better utilize available resources through niche partitioning; genetic diversity within species provides adaptation potential; and species interactions create complex networks that resist cascade effects when individual components fail. In agricultural contexts, biodiversity provides natural pest control through predator-prey relationships and reduces pathogen spread through barriers in mixed plantings. Polycultures (multiple crop species grown together) often show higher total productivity than monocultures due to complementary resource use and facilitative interactions. Biodiversity also represents a vast genetic library containing potential solutions to human challengesâmany pharmaceuticals derive from natural compounds, while wild crop relatives provide genes for breeding disease-resistant varieties. Despite these benefits, global biodiversity is declining at unprecedented rates due to habitat destruction, overexploitation, pollution, invasive species, and climate change, with an estimated one million species at risk of extinction.

scenario.title: Community Garden Designer
scenario.content: Students design and manage virtual community gardens where biodiversity principles determine ecosystem health and productivity. The simulation allows students to select from hundreds of plant and animal species with varying traits, functional roles, and interaction patterns. Students can arrange species in different spatial configurations, observe population dynamics over multiple seasons, and measure ecosystem services like pollination, pest control, and soil health. The system visualizes species interactions through network diagrams and highlights ecological relationships such as competition, mutualism, and predation. Interactive tools let students introduce stressors like drought, pest outbreaks, or disease, then observe how systems with different biodiversity levels respond. Challenge scenarios require students to create gardens that maximize specific outcomes like food production, climate resilience, or wildlife habitat, teaching the practical applications of biodiversity principles in designed ecosystems.

hypothesis.description: Students will analyze biodiversity effects by comparing ecosystem function across different community compositions. They will predict how species richness and functional diversity influence system resilience to disturbances, and explain the mechanisms by which biodiversity supports ecosystem services.
